sd_shadowlands.blurb: The Shadowlands is a cluster of walls at the upper end of Spearfish Canyon, in the northern Black Hills of South Dakota. Sport routes make up most of it, mainly 5.10 to 5.13 with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12, and a couple dozen boulder problems from V0 to V6 are mixed in. The canyon's rock is limestone, known for pocketed face climbing, and the Shadowlands is recommended for summer. Shade matters: at The Green Mile one wall never sees daylight while the other gets sun in the early afternoon. Delicacy Wall, Slim Shady Wall, Court House Wall and Wall of Wow carry the most climbs.

tn_denny_cove.blurb: Denny Cove is a long cliffline of sandstone in South Cumberland State Park, near Jasper and Foster Falls in southeast Tennessee, about half an hour from Chattanooga. Almost all of it is sport climbing, with a small amount of trad, and the grades are steep: 5.11 and 5.12 dominate, with a thinner spread of easier and harder routes either side. The rock quality swings from blocky and chunky to firm, high-quality panels, and the terrain runs from steep, overhanging walls and roofs to technical faces, slabs and a few cracks. Denny East is the larger sector. Denny West holds a concentration of more moderate routes, a trad zone and a shorter approach.

ar_jamestown_crag.blurb: Jamestown Crag is a sandstone bluff area in northeast Arkansas near Batesville, with bluffs and a valley below. Sport routes dominate, with a smaller amount of trad and some bouldering. Grades run from easy 5.5 to 5.12, but most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with the peak at 5.10, so it suits a wide range of abilities. The boulders go from V0 to V4. Natural Disaster Area and Amateur Route Area have the most routes, followed by Game Wall and Never Never Land, and a small boulder field and several small walls round it out.

co_lincoln_creek.blurb: Lincoln Creek is a side valley off the Independence Pass road east of Aspen, at around 9,600 feet, mixing boulder problems, trad and a smaller amount of sport climbing. Bouldering and trad make up most of it, with boulder grades mainly V0 to V5 and routes mostly from 5.7 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 and 5.11. The pass around it is a summer area, with granite mixed with gneiss. Crags include Sunset Cliff, Phat City, Reese's Pieces and Lincoln Creek Cliff. Reese's Pieces is a west-facing band high above the road, while Sunset Cantina is a moderate crag with jugs and protectable cracks in the 5.7 to 5.9 range.

co_grand_county_fraser_valley.blurb: Grand County and the Fraser Valley cover scattered crags north of Berthoud Pass and west of the Continental Divide, mostly within Arapaho National Forest, at around 9,000 feet. The main crags are gneiss and modest in size. Sport routes make up the bulk, mostly 5.6 to 5.12 and centred on 5.10, with some bouldering at Vasquez Road, B-Lot Boulder and Grand Lake, plus a little trad. Hurd Creek Crag has the most routes, around 50 single-pitch sport lines of 30 to 60 feet, and it generally faces southwest, so it is sunny and warm. The valley is drier than might be expected, the sun is strong, and flies and mosquitoes are common.

co_upper_boulderfield_area.blurb: The Upper Boulderfield Area is on Independence Pass in Colorado, about 11 miles up the highway from Aspen at roughly 10,000 feet. It combines bouldering right beside the road with small crags up the hillside, mostly sport routes, with some trad and a few top-ropes. The altitude keeps it cool, making it a good choice except on the hottest summer days. Sport routes run mainly from 5.8 to 5.12, centred on 5.10, and boulder problems run from V0 to V6. Upper Boulderfield, also called Bulldog Boulders, is the largest zone, followed by Upper Bulldog Cliff, Turkey Rock and Pitbull Cliff. Lower Bulldog Cliff is granite and faces south.
